source.title: SAE Interventions are Unreliable: Post-Intervention Recovery of Suppressed Behavior
source.authors: Mingyu Cui; Li Shen; Xing-Yi Yang

page_placements.theme: Selected SAE features need not form causal bottlenecks

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some equation and PDF-conversion formatting artifacts appear, but the relevant results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper cites the IOI circuit work and tests IOI behavior, but its intervention targets SAE features rather than the claimed attention-head circuit. It does not test the circuit, its head classes, or the claim's criteria.
record.gate_note: The IOI experiment is a behavior-recovery test after clamping SAE features selected by positive attribution to the IO-minus-subject logit difference. It does not ablate, patch, or evaluate the 26-head circuit. The paper reports lower activation drift, lower decode drift, and fewer reactivated positive features for encoder-projected recovery, but gives no numerical values for those comparisons in the text.
record.test_reason: The study uses the IOI task (IO-minus-S logit difference in GPT-2 Small) as a readout for its own SAE-clamp recovery diagnostic. It never ablates, patches or identifies attention heads, head classes or circuit criteria. Its only IOI results concern its own method's recovery rate, so it relies on the task as a tool and tests none of V1–V6. The record's 'cites_only/T6' undersells this: the paper runs IOI experiments, but on SAE features, not on the claimed circuit.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that SAE feature clamps act as causal handles but not complete behavioral bottlenecks: suppressed behavior, including IOI in GPT-2 Small, is recoverable from the defended residual state. In the refusal setting, recovery is carried mainly by the SAE reconstruction residual.
record.recipe_differences: The study clamps SAE features selected by attribution and optimizes residual perturbations to recover behavior. It does not apply the original head-circuit ablation and patching procedure.

fits_no_version.finding: In GPT-2 Small, IOI decisions suppressed by clamping SAE features attributed to the IO-minus-S logit difference were restored on all 37 valid flips by residual perturbation. This held both unconstrained and with updates projected away from the encoder directions; the projected variant had a 0.016 reactivated-feature fraction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A residual-SAE feature clamp on IOI-attributed features is not a complete bottleneck for GPT-2 Small's IOI behavior. The behavior can be recovered through directions outside the clamped features.

record.problems: The IOI result is conditioned on 37 valid flips and has no reported uncertainty interval. The study tests SAE-feature interventions, not the claimed attention-head circuit.
record.rows_left_out: No other results bear on the specified circuit claim. Results for TPP, WMDP-Bio, refusal recovery, and refusal feature-set sweeps concern other behaviors or settings.

untested.parts: All of it: the 26 heads, the 7 classes, and the faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria.
All of it: no name-mover ablation and no measure of head-level self-repair. The recovery reported is optimizer-driven residual perturbation, not backup heads.
All of it: only GPT-2 Small is used for IOI, with no other models, checkpoints or tasks.
All of it: no comparison of circuit-finding methods.
All of it: no variation of ablation type, metric or prompt distribution for circuit evaluation.
All of it: no comparison of name orders, templates or numbers of names.

missing.what: Reactivated-feature fraction of 0.016 for encoder-projected IOI recovery (not recorded in R2's value; out of scope for all versions).

record.verdict_notes: The relation is changed from cites_only/T6 to uses_without_test/T4, because the paper runs IOI as a 'circuit-level sanity check' for its own diagnostic. No verdicts are given, since no row measures the attention-head circuit. The study's recovery phenomenon should not be read as evidence for V2 backup heads: it is optimized perturbation rather than spontaneous compensation by heads.

versions.untested_parts: The 26-head, seven-class circuit, its stated roles, and faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria are not tested.
No main name-mover heads are ablated or tested for self-repair.
No other models, sizes, checkpoints, or tasks are tested for reuse of the claimed head classes.
The study does not compare circuit-finding methods, head ablation types, or circuit evaluation metrics.
It does not vary the circuit evaluation's ablation, metric, or IOI prompt distribution.
The IOI recovery experiment does not compare name orders, templates, or numbers of names.

relation.reason: The original circuit paper is cited as reference [22], but its head classes, components and circuit criteria are neither used nor evaluated.

tranche.reason: Section 5.3 uses the IOI behavioral task to evaluate SAE-clamp recovery. It neither tests nor uses the claimed attention-head circuit; using the task alone does not establish T4.
